title: Teaching Aptitude
overview: Is unit mein teaching ka concept, objectives, levels (memory, understanding, reflective), learner ki characteristics, teaching ko affect karne wale factors, methods (teacher-centred vs learner-centred, offline vs online jaise SWAYAM, MOOCs), support system (traditional, modern, ICT) aur evaluation (CBCS, CBT) aata hai. NET mein 5 questions aate hain, zyada tar statement-based, match-the-following aur 'best teaching practice' wale sawal.

topics.title: Teaching: Concept and Nature
points: Teaching is a planned, purposeful, tripolar process involving teacher, learner and the social environment/curriculum (tripolar view of John Dewey; bipolar view of John Adams: teacher and learner).
Morrison (1934): teaching is an intimate contact between a more mature personality and a less mature one, designed to further the education of the latter.
N.L. Gage (1963): teaching is a form of interpersonal influence aimed at changing the behaviour potential of another person.
Burton: teaching is the stimulation, guidance, direction and encouragement of learning.
Nature of teaching: both an art and a science; a social and interactive process; goal-oriented; can be observed, analysed and improved (it is modifiable).
Phases of teaching (P.W. Jackson, Life in Classrooms, 1968): pre-active (planning), interactive (actual classroom), post-active (evaluation and reflection).
Teaching and learning are related but not identical: teaching is the means, learning is the end; good teaching is judged by learning outcomes.
Robert Glaser's Basic Teaching Model (1962): instructional objectives, entering behaviour, instructional procedures, performance assessment.
Joyce and Weil, Models of Teaching (1972): four families - information processing, social interaction, personal, behavioural systems.
Teaching is the most effective when it is learner-centred, democratic, interactive and linked to real life (NET favours these options).

topics.title: Objectives of Teaching and Bloom's Taxonomy
points: Objectives of teaching: bringing desirable change in behaviour across cognitive (knowing), affective (feeling) and conative/psychomotor (doing) domains.
Benjamin Bloom and associates, Taxonomy of Educational Objectives: Handbook I, Cognitive Domain (1956).
Original cognitive levels (lowest to highest): Knowledge, Comprehension, Application, Analysis, Synthesis, Evaluation.
Revised taxonomy by Lorin Anderson and David Krathwohl (2001): Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyse, Evaluate, Create (verbs, and Create is now the top).
Affective domain (Krathwohl, Bloom and Masia, 1964): Receiving, Responding, Valuing, Organisation, Characterisation by a value (complex).
Psychomotor domain was not completed by Bloom; versions by R.H. Dave (1970: Imitation, Manipulation, Precision, Articulation, Naturalisation), Elizabeth Simpson (1972) and Anita Harrow (1972).
Aims are broad and long-term; objectives are specific; learning outcomes are measurable statements of what the learner can do (use action verbs like list, explain, design).
Teaching objectives in higher education: knowledge creation, critical thinking, problem solving, skill development, values and employability.

topics.title: Levels of Teaching: Memory, Understanding and Reflective
points: Three levels in ascending order: Memory level, Understanding level, Reflective level.

Memory level: lowest, 'thoughtless' teaching based on rote learning and recall; associated with Herbart; Herbartian steps: preparation, presentation, comparison/association, generalisation, application.

Understanding level: 'thoughtful' teaching; learner grasps principles, facts and relationships; associated with Henry C. Morrison; Morrison's steps: exploration, presentation, assimilation, organisation, recitation.
Reflective level: highest, 'upper thoughtful' or problem-centred teaching; develops reasoning, critical and creative thinking; associated with Morris L. Bigge and Maurice P. Hunt.
At reflective level the learner identifies a problem, frames hypotheses, tests them and reaches conclusions (like scientific method); classroom is open and democratic.
Memory level is a prerequisite for understanding level, which in turn is the prerequisite for reflective level.
Role of teacher: dominant at memory level, shared at understanding level, least dominant (facilitator) at reflective level.
Evaluation: memory level by recall/objective tests; understanding level by objective plus essay questions; reflective level by essay-type, problem-solving and open-ended questions.

topics.title: Characteristics and Basic Requirements of Effective Teaching
points: Effective teaching is planned, purposeful, learner-centred, interactive, democratic, diagnostic and remedial, and uses feedback.
Basic requirements: mastery of subject, clear objectives, lesson planning, good communication, classroom management, motivation, suitable methods and aids, and evaluation.

Maxims of teaching: known to unknown, simple to complex, concrete to abstract, particular to general, whole to part, analysis to synthesis, empirical to rational, psychological to logical, induction to deduction.

Teaching skills are practised through micro-teaching: developed at Stanford University (early 1960s, Dwight W. Allen and colleagues); in India D.D. Tiwari (1967, Central Pedagogical Institute, Allahabad).

Micro-teaching cycle: plan - teach - feedback - re-plan - re-teach - re-feedback; Indian model: teach 6 min, feedback 6 min, re-plan 12 min, re-teach 6 min, re-feedback 6 min (36 minutes); 5-10 students.
Flanders' Interaction Analysis Category System (Ned Flanders, 1960s-1970): 10 categories - 7 teacher talk (1-4 indirect, 5-7 direct), 2 student talk (8-9), 1 silence or confusion (10).
Teacher qualities valued in NET options: patience, empathy, impartiality, enthusiasm, openness to questions, using examples, and being a role model.
A good teacher is a facilitator and guide, not just an information giver; encourages questioning and self-learning.

topics.title: Learner's Characteristics: Adolescent and Adult Learners
points: Higher education learners are late adolescents and adults; characteristics are studied under academic, social, emotional and cognitive heads.
G. Stanley Hall (Adolescence, 1904) called adolescence a period of 'storm and stress'.
Cognitive: adolescents reach Piaget's formal operational stage (about 11 years onward) - abstract, hypothetical and logical thinking.
Emotional: mood swings, need for identity and independence; Erik Erikson's stage 'identity vs role confusion' (about 12-18 years).
Social: strong peer influence, need for acceptance, idealism, interest in social causes.
Academic: curiosity, need for relevance, career orientation, varied interests and capacities.
Adult learning = Andragogy, popularised by Malcolm Knowles (The Modern Practice of Adult Education, 1970); pedagogy is the teaching of children.
Knowles' andragogy assumptions: self-directed self-concept, rich experience as a resource, readiness linked to life roles, problem-centred orientation, internal motivation, need to know why.
Heutagogy (Stewart Hase and Chris Kenyon, 2000): self-determined learning, learner decides what and how to learn.

topics.title: Individual Differences and Learning Styles
points: Individual differences: learners differ in intelligence, aptitude, interest, attitude, learning style, pace, personality, socio-economic background.
Causes: heredity and environment (nature and nurture) interacting.

Howard Gardner, Frames of Mind (1983): Multiple Intelligences - linguistic, logical-mathematical, spatial, musical, bodily-kinaesthetic, interpersonal, intrapersonal; naturalist added later (1990s) as the eighth.
Neil Fleming's VARK model: Visual, Aural, Read/write, Kinaesthetic learners.

David Kolb, Experiential Learning (1984): cycle of concrete experience, reflective observation, abstract conceptualisation, active experimentation; styles - diverging, assimilating, converging, accommodating.
Lev Vygotsky: Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD) and scaffolding - learning with help of a more knowledgeable other.
Teacher response to differences: differentiated instruction, flexible grouping, remedial teaching for slow learners, enrichment for gifted, varied methods and aids.
Inclusive education: teaching all learners including those with disabilities in the same classroom; the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 supports it.

topics.title: Factors Affecting Teaching
points: Teacher factors: subject mastery, teaching skills, personality, attitude, motivation, communication, experience, mental and physical health.
Learner factors: prior knowledge, motivation, attention, intelligence, aptitude, readiness, health, socio-economic and family background.
Support material: textbooks, reference books, e-content, audio-visual aids, study guides, question banks.
Instructional facilities: classroom space, seating, lighting, ventilation, laboratory, library, ICT equipment, internet.
Learning environment: physical (noise, temperature) and psycho-social (classroom climate, teacher-student rapport, peer relations, discipline).
Institution: leadership, policies, culture, resources, class size, timetable, academic freedom, evaluation system.
Motivation: intrinsic (from within, interest) is more lasting than extrinsic (rewards, marks).
A positive, democratic and non-threatening climate improves participation and learning (NET's preferred answer).

topics.title: Teacher-Centred vs Learner-Centred Methods
points: Teacher-centred (autocratic) methods: lecture, demonstration, tutorial (teacher-led), team teaching, programmed instruction (teacher designs everything); teacher is the main actor, learners are passive.

Learner-centred (democratic/constructivist) methods: discussion, seminar, project, problem-solving, case study, role play, brainstorming, inquiry, discovery, field trip, flipped classroom, cooperative learning.
Lecture method is the most widely used in higher education; good for large classes and covering content, weak on interaction.
Project method: William H. Kilpatrick (1918), based on John Dewey's pragmatism ('learning by doing').
Heuristic method: H.E. Armstrong - learner discovers as a researcher.
Dalton Plan: Helen Parkhurst (1920) - individual contracts/assignments; Keller Plan or Personalised System of Instruction: Fred S. Keller (1968).
Programmed instruction: B.F. Skinner's linear programming (operant conditioning); Norman Crowder's branching programming.
Brainstorming: Alex Osborn (popularised in Applied Imagination, 1953) - free generation of ideas without criticism.
Case method: Harvard Law School under Christopher Langdell (1870s); Jigsaw cooperative technique: Elliot Aronson (1971).

Seminar: a paper presented and discussed; Symposium: several experts speak on aspects of one topic; Panel discussion: experts discuss before an audience under a moderator; Workshop: hands-on, product-oriented.

topics.title: Offline vs Online Methods: SWAYAM, SWAYAM Prabha, MOOCs
points: Offline methods: face-to-face classroom teaching, labs, printed material; Online: internet-based, synchronous (live) or asynchronous (recorded); Blended learning mixes both.
MOOC = Massive Open Online Course; the term was coined in 2008 by Dave Cormier (with Bryan Alexander) for a course by George Siemens and Stephen Downes.
cMOOCs are connectivist (networked learning); xMOOCs are structured, video-lecture based (Coursera, edX, Udacity - all 2012, the 'Year of the MOOC').
SWAYAM: Study Webs of Active-Learning for Young Aspiring Minds; Government of India (MHRD, now Ministry of Education) MOOC platform launched on 9 July 2017.
SWAYAM four quadrants: (1) video lectures, (2) e-content/reading material, (3) self-assessment tests and quizzes, (4) discussion forum for doubts.

SWAYAM national coordinators include AICTE, NPTEL (engineering), UGC (non-technical PG), CEC (undergraduate), NCERT and NIOS (school), IGNOU (out-of-school), IIM Bangalore (management), NITTTR (teacher training).
UGC Credit Framework for Online Learning Courses through SWAYAM: credit transfer allowed (now up to 40% of credits in a programme per semester as per 2021 regulations).
SWAYAM Prabha: group of DTH channels launched 9 July 2017 (started with 32 channels) telecasting educational content 24x7 via GSAT satellite; free to air.

Other ICT initiatives: NPTEL (2003, IITs and IISc), e-PG Pathshala (UGC-INFLIBNET), National Digital Library of India (IIT Kharagpur), Shodhganga (theses, INFLIBNET), DIKSHA (2017, school teachers), NMEICT (2009), Virtual Labs, Spoken Tutorial (IIT Bombay).
Advantages of online: flexibility, scale, access, self-pace; limitations: digital divide, less interaction, high dropout, need for self-discipline.

topics.title: Teaching Support System: Traditional, Modern and ICT-based
points: Traditional aids: chalkboard/blackboard, textbook, charts, maps, models, flannel board, bulletin board, real objects (realia).
Modern aids: overhead projector (OHP), slide projector, film, radio, television, audio and video recorders, LCD projector.
ICT-based aids: computers, internet, PowerPoint, interactive/smart boards, LMS (e.g. Moodle), video conferencing, e-books, simulations, virtual labs, mobile apps, AI tools.
Aids are classified as audio (radio, podcast), visual (chart, slide) and audio-visual (TV, film, video).
Projected aids: OHP, slides, LCD; non-projected aids: chalkboard, charts, models.
Edgar Dale's Cone of Experience (1946): from direct purposeful experience (base, most concrete) to verbal symbols (top, most abstract).
Aids should be relevant, simple, visible, accurate and used at the right time; they support but do not replace the teacher.
Flipped classroom: learners study content (videos) at home and do activities/problem solving in class.
Hardware approach (machines, equipment) vs software approach (programmed material, teaching strategies) - both part of educational technology.

topics.title: Evaluation: Elements and Types
points: Measurement is quantitative (scores); assessment collects information; evaluation adds value judgement (quantitative plus qualitative description and judgement).
Ralph Tyler's triangle: educational objectives, learning experiences, evaluation are interrelated (Basic Principles of Curriculum and Instruction, 1949).
Michael Scriven (1967) coined the terms formative evaluation (during instruction, to improve it) and summative evaluation (at the end, to grade/certify).
Placement evaluation: before instruction, to judge entry behaviour; Diagnostic evaluation: to find persistent learning difficulties and their causes, followed by remedial teaching.
Norm-referenced test: compares a learner with others (rank, percentile); Criterion-referenced test: compares with a fixed standard or mastery level (terms from Robert Glaser, 1963).
Characteristics of a good test: validity (measures what it claims), reliability (consistency), objectivity (free from examiner bias), usability/practicability, discrimination power.
A test can be reliable without being valid, but a valid test must be reliable.
Continuous and Comprehensive Evaluation (CCE): continuous (regular, formative and summative) and comprehensive (scholastic plus co-scholastic areas).
Tools: tests (essay, short answer, objective), rating scale, checklist, observation, interview, portfolio, rubrics, anecdotal record.

topics.title: Evaluation in Choice Based Credit System (CBCS)
points: UGC introduced CBCS guidelines for higher education in 2015 (implemented from academic year 2015-16).
Semester system with credits; students choose courses from core, elective and skill-based courses, with a cafeteria approach.
Course types: Core courses, Elective courses (Discipline Specific Elective, Generic Elective), Ability Enhancement Compulsory Courses (AECC), Skill Enhancement Courses (SEC).
One credit generally = one hour of lecture or tutorial per week in a semester, or two hours of practical per week.
UGC 10-point grading: O (Outstanding) 10, A+ (Excellent) 9, A (Very Good) 8, B+ (Good) 7, B (Above Average) 6, C (Average) 5, P (Pass) 4, F (Fail) 0, Ab (Absent) 0.
SGPA = sum of (course credits x grade points) / total credits in a semester; CGPA is the same computed over all semesters.
Relative grading is based on the performance of the whole class; absolute grading on fixed marks ranges.
NEP 2020 builds on CBCS with multiple entry and exit, Academic Bank of Credits (ABC, launched July 2021) and the four-year undergraduate programme.
Advantages of CBCS: flexibility, mobility between institutions, interdisciplinary choice, continuous internal assessment.

topics.title: Computer Based Testing and Innovations in Evaluation
points: Computer Based Test (CBT): candidates answer on a computer; quick, accurate, secure results; NTA (set up in 2017) conducts UGC NET in CBT mode since December 2018.
Computer Adaptive Testing (CAT): the next item depends on the previous answer - difficulty goes up after a correct answer and down after a wrong one; based on Item Response Theory.
Advantages of CBT: instant scoring, item randomisation, multiple test sessions, item banking, less paper; issues: infrastructure, digital familiarity, technical glitches.

Innovations: open-book examination, online/remote proctoring, on-demand examination, e-portfolio, rubrics, peer and self assessment, grading instead of marks, question banks, continuous internal assessment.
Rubric: a scoring guide with criteria and performance levels, increases objectivity in grading essays and projects.
360-degree evaluation: feedback from teachers, peers, self and others.
Item analysis: difficulty index (proportion correct) and discrimination index (how well an item separates high and low scorers).
OMR (Optical Mark Recognition) sheets are machine-scored paper tests; CBT replaces them in many national exams.
Learning analytics on LMS data helps track progress and give early warning to teachers.

terms.hindi: बच्चों को पढ़ाने की कला और विज्ञान
terms.net: The art and science of teaching, traditionally the teaching of children, in which the teacher decides what, when and how is learned.

terms.hindi: बड़ों (वयस्कों) को पढ़ाने का तरीका
terms.net: The method and practice of teaching adult learners; popularised by Malcolm Knowles (1970) on assumptions of self-direction, experience, readiness, problem orientation and internal motivation.

terms.hindi: खुद तय करके सीखना
terms.net: Self-determined learning in which the learner decides what and how to learn; proposed by Stewart Hase and Chris Kenyon (2000).

terms.hindi: सोचने-समझने वाला क्षेत्र
terms.net: The domain of educational objectives concerned with knowledge and intellectual skills; Bloom's Taxonomy, Handbook I (1956).

terms.hindi: भावना, रुचि और मूल्यों वाला क्षेत्र
terms.net: The domain of objectives concerned with feelings, attitudes, interests and values; classified by Krathwohl, Bloom and Masia (1964).

terms.hindi: हाथ-पैर से करने वाले कौशल
terms.net: The domain of objectives dealing with physical movement and motor skills; taxonomies by Dave (1970), Simpson (1972) and Harrow (1972).

terms.hindi: वर्गीकरण
terms.net: A hierarchical classification; in education, Bloom's hierarchy of learning objectives from simple to complex.

terms.hindi: छोटी क्लास में छोटा पाठ पढ़ाकर एक कौशल का अभ्यास
terms.net: A scaled-down teaching encounter (5-10 learners, 5-10 minutes, one skill) with feedback, developed at Stanford University in the early 1960s.

terms.hindi: सोच-विचार और समस्या पर आधारित पढ़ाई
terms.net: The highest level of teaching (Hunt), problem-centred, developing critical and creative thinking; also a teacher's habit of reflecting on own practice.

terms.hindi: पढ़ाई के दौरान सुधार के लिए जाँच
terms.net: Evaluation carried out during instruction to monitor progress and improve teaching and learning; term coined by Michael Scriven (1967).

terms.hindi: अंत में अंक/ग्रेड देने वाली जाँच
terms.net: Evaluation at the end of a course or unit to judge overall achievement, certify or grade; term coined by Michael Scriven (1967).

terms.hindi: कमज़ोरी और उसका कारण पता करना
terms.net: Evaluation to identify persistent learning difficulties and their causes so that remedial teaching can be given.

terms.hindi: शुरू में स्तर तय करने वाली जाँच
terms.net: Evaluation before instruction to determine entry behaviour and place the learner at the right level or group.

terms.hindi: दूसरों से तुलना करके परखना
terms.net: A test that interprets a score by comparing the learner with a norm group (rank, percentile).

terms.hindi: तय मानक से तुलना
terms.net: A test that interprets a score against a fixed standard of mastery, not against other learners; term from Robert Glaser (1963).

terms.hindi: जो मापना है वही मापे
terms.net: The degree to which a test measures what it claims to measure.

terms.hindi: बार-बार मापने पर एक जैसा परिणाम
terms.net: The consistency or stability of test scores over repeated measurement.

terms.hindi: जाँचने वाले की पसंद-नापसंद का असर न हो
terms.net: The extent to which scoring is free from the personal judgement or bias of the examiner.

terms.hindi: अंक देने की तय मापदंड-सारणी
terms.net: A scoring guide listing criteria and levels of performance used to evaluate work consistently.

terms.hindi: विषय चुनने की आज़ादी वाली क्रेडिट प्रणाली
terms.net: Choice Based Credit System, introduced by UGC (2015), allowing students to choose core, elective and skill courses with credits and grade points.

terms.hindi: एक सेमेस्टर का औसत ग्रेड अंक
terms.net: Semester Grade Point Average: sum of (credits x grade points) of all courses in a semester divided by total credits.

terms.hindi: सभी सेमेस्टर का कुल औसत ग्रेड
terms.net: Cumulative Grade Point Average computed over all semesters of a programme.

terms.hindi: बहुत बड़ी संख्या के लिए खुला ऑनलाइन कोर्स
terms.net: Massive Open Online Course; term coined in 2008 by Dave Cormier; offered on platforms such as SWAYAM, Coursera and edX.

terms.hindi: भारत सरकार का मुफ्त ऑनलाइन कोर्स पोर्टल
terms.net: Study Webs of Active-Learning for Young Aspiring Minds, India's MOOC platform launched 9 July 2017, built on four quadrants.

terms.hindi: शिक्षा के मुफ्त डीटीएच टीवी चैनल
terms.net: Group of educational DTH channels launched 9 July 2017 (initially 32) telecasting curriculum content 24x7.

terms.hindi: आमने-सामने और ऑनलाइन दोनों मिलाकर पढ़ाई
terms.net: An approach combining face-to-face classroom teaching with online learning.

terms.hindi: घर पर वीडियो से पढ़ो, क्लास में अभ्यास
terms.net: A model in which learners study instructional content at home and use class time for activities, discussion and problem solving.

terms.hindi: एक ही समय पर लाइव पढ़ाई
terms.net: Online learning in which teacher and learners interact at the same time (live class, webinar).

terms.hindi: अपने समय पर रिकॉर्डेड पढ़ाई
terms.net: Online learning in which participants access material at different times (recorded video, forum).

terms.hindi: सीखते समय दिया गया अस्थायी सहारा
terms.net: Temporary support given to a learner to perform a task within the Zone of Proximal Development, withdrawn gradually; concept from Vygotsky's theory (term by Wood, Bruner and Ross, 1976).

terms.hindi: जो बच्चा मदद से कर सके पर अकेले नहीं
terms.net: Vygotsky's term for the gap between what a learner can do alone and what can be done with guidance of a more knowledgeable other.

terms.hindi: बुद्धि के कई प्रकार
terms.net: Howard Gardner's theory (Frames of Mind, 1983) that intelligence has several distinct forms such as linguistic, logical-mathematical and interpersonal.

terms.hindi: पढ़ाने के सूत्र/नियम
terms.net: Guiding principles of teaching such as known to unknown, simple to complex, concrete to abstract and particular to general.

terms.hindi: कक्षा में बातचीत का विश्लेषण
terms.net: Systematic observation of classroom verbal behaviour; Flanders' 10-category system (FIACS).

terms.hindi: जवाब के हिसाब से अगला सवाल आसान या कठिन
terms.net: Computer-based testing in which the difficulty of each next item depends on the candidate's responses, based on Item Response Theory.

terms.hindi: हर सवाल की कठिनता और भेद क्षमता जाँचना
terms.net: Statistical review of test items using difficulty index and discrimination index.

terms.hindi: कमज़ोर छात्रों के लिए सुधार की पढ़ाई
terms.net: Corrective instruction given after diagnostic evaluation to remove learning difficulties.

terms.hindi: अनुभव का शंकु: ठोस से अमूर्त
terms.net: Dale's Cone of Experience (1946), arranging learning experiences from direct purposeful experience (concrete) at the base to verbal symbols (abstract) at the top.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct ascending order of levels of teaching?
mcqs.exp: Memory is lowest, reflective is highest.

mcqs.q: The reflective level of teaching is associated with:
mcqs.exp: Herbart - memory, Morrison - understanding, Hunt - reflective.

mcqs.q: Who coined the terms 'formative' and 'summative' evaluation?
mcqs.exp: Scriven used the terms in 1967.

mcqs.q: In the revised Bloom's taxonomy (2001), the highest cognitive level is:
mcqs.exp: Anderson and Krathwohl put Create at the top.

mcqs.q: SWAYAM was launched in the year:
mcqs.exp: Launched on 9 July 2017.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT one of the four quadrants of SWAYAM?
mcqs.exp: The quadrants are video, e-content, self-assessment and discussion forum.

mcqs.q: A test that compares a student's performance with that of other students is:
mcqs.exp: Norm-referenced tests rank against a group.

mcqs.q: Evaluation done to identify the causes of persistent learning difficulty is called:
mcqs.exp: Diagnosis finds causes; remedial teaching follows.

mcqs.q: The concept of 'Andragogy' is associated with:
mcqs.exp: Knowles popularised andragogy for adult learners.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a learner-centred method?
mcqs.exp: Project method involves learners actively; lecture and demonstration are teacher-centred.

mcqs.q: The Project method was developed by:
mcqs.exp: Kilpatrick (1918), following Dewey.

mcqs.q: In UGC's 10-point grading scale under CBCS, grade 'A+' stands for:
mcqs.exp: O=10 Outstanding, A+=9 Excellent, A=8 Very Good.

mcqs.q: A test that gives consistent results on repeated administration is said to have:
mcqs.exp: Consistency = reliability.

mcqs.q: Micro-teaching was first developed at:
mcqs.exp: Stanford, early 1960s.

mcqs.q: Which phase of teaching includes lesson planning?
mcqs.exp: Jackson: planning is the pre-active phase.

mcqs.q:
Match the following:
List I: (a) Memory level (b) Understanding level (c) Reflective level (d) Programmed instruction
List II: (i) Morrison (ii) Skinner (iii) Herbart (iv) Hunt
mcqs.exp: Herbart, Morrison, Hunt, Skinner.

mcqs.q:
Match the following:
List I: (a) Remember (b) Analyse (c) Valuing (d) Naturalisation
List II: (i) Psychomotor domain (ii) Affective domain (iii) Lowest cognitive level (revised) (iv) Higher cognitive level
mcqs.exp: Remember is lowest; Valuing is affective; Naturalisation is Dave's psychomotor level.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): Reflective level teaching is the highest level of teaching. Reason (R): It develops problem-solving, critical and creative thinking in learners.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
mcqs.exp: Both true; R explains why it is highest.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): A valid test is always reliable. Reason (R): Reliability is a necessary condition for validity.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
mcqs.exp: Without consistency a test cannot measure accurately, so validity needs reliability.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): Lecture method is learner-centred. Reason (R): Lecture method is economical for large classes.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
mcqs.exp: Lecture is teacher-centred; but it is economical for large groups.

mcqs.q: Arrange in chronological order: (a) Bloom's cognitive taxonomy (b) Revised Bloom's taxonomy (c) Krathwohl's affective taxonomy (d) Launch of SWAYAM
In Flanders' Interaction Analysis, category 10 refers to:
mcqs.exp: Category 10 is silence/confusion.

mcqs.q: Who said teaching is 'an intimate contact between a more mature personality and a less mature one'?
mcqs.exp: H.C. Morrison (1934).

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an ICT-based teaching support?
mcqs.exp: LMS like Moodle is ICT-based.

mcqs.q: Edgar Dale's Cone of Experience places at its base:
mcqs.exp: The base is the most concrete experience.

mcqs.q: In Computer Adaptive Testing:
options: The difficulty of the next question depends on the previous response
All candidates get identical questions in the same order
Results are declared after manual checking
mcqs.exp: CAT adapts item difficulty to responses.

mcqs.q: Which statement about formative evaluation is correct?
options: It is used mainly for certification
It compares students with national norms
It is conducted only at the end of the course
It is conducted during instruction to improve learning
mcqs.exp: Formative = during instruction, for improvement.

mcqs.q: 'Storm and stress' as a description of adolescence is associated with:
mcqs.exp: Hall, Adolescence (1904).

mcqs.q: Which of these is NOT a characteristic of adult learners according to Knowles?
options: Dependent on the teacher for direction
mcqs.exp: Adults are self-directed, not dependent.

mcqs.q: Which maxim of teaching is wrongly stated?
mcqs.exp: The correct maxim is concrete to abstract.
